newsitem.title: USA: Pennzoil, Coastal hit with discrimination suits.
newsitem.headline: Pennzoil, Coastal hit with discrimination suits.

text.p: Two major oil companies, Pennzoil Co. and Coastal Corp., have been sued for racial discrimination in federal court in two that which echo last year's successful claim against Texaco Inc.
Both oil companies are denying the accusations.

The New York law firm Bernstein, Litowitz, Berger & Grossmann, which handled the suit against Texaco, said Tuesday its clients were seeking at least $400 million from Coastal and $300 million from Pennzoil in the suits filed in U.S. District Court in Houston.
In November, Texaco agreed to settle a highly publicised racial discrimination suit by paying $176.1 million and establishing an "equality and tolerance" task force.

"In the Pennzoil case we represent 11 African-American employees alleging race discrimination similar to what we alleged in Texaco, lack of opportunities for advancement, promotion and salaries," Daniel Berger, a partner at the law firm said.
The plaintiffs will seek class action status from the court for their complaint in July.
In the Coastal case, there are 10 plaintiffs, whose allegations cover similar complaints.

"Based on our investigations so far, we do not believe any of these allegations will be substantiated, except one allegation relating to a co-worker who made racist remarks to one of our employees," Coastal said in a statement.
Coastal said that the employee who made the remarks had been fired.
Pennzoil declined to comment other than saying it "would vigorously defend the action."
However, Berger said that the two cases indicated that the "redneck" attitude of oil companies still prevailed.
"There are 400 to 500 African American employees in Coastal out of 8,000, they are all lumped at the bottom of the paygrade scale," said Berger.
Coastal declined to confirm or deny the figures, but said in its reply to the court that employees "receive fair and equal treatment regardless of race, or any other protected status."
Berger said that these cases were not examples of black employees saying "me too" after the success against Texaco.
"We would not have taken these cases without the evidence. The policies of Penzoil and Coastal have resulted in African American employees faring horribly," he said.
He noted that there were no black board members at Coastal and one recent appointee at Pennzoil.

"Coastal has never had a minority on the board. If you are dealing with a good old boys club where the directors are all white males it is no surprise that African Americans do not do well," said Berger.
Most analysts declined to comment on the issue, but one who spoke on condition of anonymity said: "This has the potential to be a significant event for both companies."
